sentences.text: The species name refers to the La Amarga Formation and the animal's small size.
The maxilla surface features heavy sculpting, most pronounced along the mid-section.
The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in 1984 in the lower La Amarga Formation alongside the sauropod dinosaur Amargasaurus.
It belongs to the subclass Diapsida.
It belongs to the infraclass Archosauromorpha.
It belongs to the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
The type species is A. minor, described by Chiappe in 1988.
It is currently associated with either the clade Pepesuchinae or Itasuchidae.
Phylogenetic studies place it in a polytomy with Caririsuchus, Itasuchus, and Roxochampsa.
It was considered a member of the enigmatic family Trematochampsidae.
Fossils date from the Barremian to Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
The time range is estimated from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
It inhabited a terrestrial Early Cretaceous environment in the Neuquén basin characterized by braided rivers, lakes, and alluvial plains.
Taxonomy varies between authors regarding the split of Peirosauridae into subfamilies and their relationships.
